title: Protocol to optimize the biobanking of ovarian cancer organoids by accommodating patient-specific differences in stemness potential
protocol: Transfer the tissue to a Petri dish within a cell culture Laminar flow.
Wash extensively in PBS without Ca++, Mg++.
Homogenize with scissors.
Soak tissue in PBS during homogenization to avoid drying out.
Mince further the remaining tissue with a scalpel for mechanical dissociation before enzymatic digestion.
Collect small fragments (3–5 mm) into Cryo tubes and perform snap freezing in liquid nitrogen.
Put 1–2 fragments into formalin for fixation (24 h).
Embed fixed fragments in paraffin for comparative staining with organoids.
Digest tissue in PBS without Ca++ and Mg++ + collagenase I (stock solution 5 U/μL, final concentration 1U/μL) + Y-27632 at 3 μM final concentration.
Incubate the digestion mixture for 1.5 hours in a 37°C water bath with sporadic vigorous vortexing every 20 minutes for 10 seconds to enhance dissociation.
Inactivate and wash the tissue with 15 mL ADF++.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 minutes, discard the supernatant, add 5 mL new ADF++, and filtrate through a cell strainer of 400 μm into a fresh 50-mL-Falcon tube.
Discard the supernatant, add 5 mL RBC Buffer, and incubate in the water bath for 5 minutes to stop lysis.
Stop lysis with 5 mL ADF++ and centrifuge for 5 minutes at 300 g.
Resuspend the pellet in 3 mL ADF++.
Count cells using a Neubauer Chamber or automatic cell counter.
Dilute the cell suspension 1:2 with Trypan blue (e.g., 10 μL of sample + 10 μL Trypan blue) for manual counting.
Fill the diluted sample in the Neubauer counting chamber and evaluate the number of cells in 4 big squares.
Calculate the cell yield per mL by averaging the number of cells per square, factoring in dilution, and multiplying by 10^4.
Seed 30,000 cells per 25 μL Cultrex in a 48-well format.
Calculate the total number of cells needed for all Cultrex wells.
Separate ADF++ cell suspension to a new tube accordingly.
Spin down the cells for 5 min at 300 g and remove the supernatant.
Add cold Cultrex at an appropriate amount (250 μL for 10 wells in 48-well format).
Distribute isolates in Cultrex droplets (25 μL) to pre-warmed empty 48-well plate.
Thoroughly mix the cells in Cultrex without creating bubbles.
Incubate the plate for a minimum of 30 min at 37°C so that Cultrex solidifies.
Add appropriate growth medium, 250 μL per well.
Seed remaining cells (1 × 10^6) to T75 Flask in 2D medium if fewer cells are available, seed in the T25 flask.
Allow cells in the flask to adhere for 3–5 days.
Do not change the medium for the first 72 h.
Image the cultures at least once per week to document long-term growth.
Select the best medium condition for long-term expansion at 14–21 days post-isolation.
Wait at least 14 days before classifying the sample as “no growth.”
Transfer cells to Cultrex BME 2 in passage 0 as soon as they reach confluency.
Do not propagate primary isolates in 2D culture by splitting.
Pool 2-3 wells per 1 stock vial for optimal biobanking.

Add 250 μL of cold ADF++ medium in a 48-well format or 500 μL in a 24-well format and thoroughly scrape the bottom of the plate with a pipette tip, pipetting up and down intermittently to ensure Cultrex is disrupted.
Transfer cell suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube, add an additional 1 mL of cold ADF++, mix, and keep on ice.
Spin down organoids for 5 min at 300 g.
Discard the supernatant; if the Cultrex layer remains visible on top of the pellet, repeat washing step.
Add 1 mL of TrypLE stored at 20°C-25°C.
Incubate in a water bath for 7-10 min.
Periodically vortex suspension for 10 s during incubation to improve dissociation efficiency.
If large cell aggregates are still present, passage the suspension 3-5 times through a 1 mL cannula with a 27G syringe.
Pass through the syringe if required using needles in the range of 23 gauge to 27 gauge as needed for dissociation efficacy.
Add 1 mL of cold ADF++ to stop the reaction.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 300 g.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in an appropriate volume of Cultrex, e.g., resuspend 50 μL parental passage in 150 μL fresh Cultrex for a 1:3 split.
Pipette up and down carefully to ensure uniform suspension.
Distribute the cell suspension to prewarmed plate.
Incubate at 37°C for a minimum of 30 min.
Add medium, 500 μL per well, after incubation.
Change medium twice weekly.
Take pictures at regular intervals for systematic comparisons between different conditions.
Make sure that ADF++ is properly cooled before harvesting the organoids.
Thoroughly perform mixing steps to ensure efficient removal of the extracellular matrix, which dissolves below 4°C.
When removing the medium in step 28, leave as little residual liquid as possible to avoid diluting Cultrex BME2 and increasing droplet fragility.
Take 1.8 mL Nunc cryovials, label them with name, passage number, kind of medium, and date of freezing.
Put labeled cryovials on ice.
Precool the freezing medium (Cryo SFM) on ice.
Add 1 mL of CryoSFM to the organoid pellet and transfer it to the cryo tubes.
Store the tubes in a precooled Mr. Frosty and place them at -80°C overnight.
Transfer the stock tubes from -80°C storage to liquid nitrogen for long-term stable storage (>2 months).
Freeze the organoids within the first week after passaging during the proliferative stage.
Perform fixing, imaging analysis 10–14 days after splitting when organoids are differentiated and reach optimal size.
Label a 15 mL falcon with prewarmed 9 mL ADF++.
Take the organoid sample out of the −80°C freezer or liquid nitrogen and transfer it to a small table container prefilled with liquid nitrogen.
Transfer the organoid suspension carefully to a 37°C warm water bath while shaking softly.
Transfer the organoid suspension drop by drop into the prepared falcon containing 9 mL ADF++ and mix carefully.
Spin down the mixture for 5 min at 300 g.
Add 3 mL of 4% PFA to the collected organoids and incubate for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Wash the organoids two times with 5 mL PBS, spinning them down for 3 min at 300 g after each wash.
Resuspend the organoids in 4 mL fresh PBS and store at 4°C until embedding.
Prewarm HistoGel (stored at −20°C) in a heat block at 65°C.
Remove supernatant from fixed organoids if sedimented, or briefly centrifuge disrupted pellets and remove PBS.
Add 100 μL of warm Histogel and pipette up and down over the organoids on Parafilm.
Transfer the firm droplet to the tissue paraffin cassette.
Cut 5–10 μm thick slices with a microtome, and mount them on slides.
Dry slides for 1 hour at 65°C.
Move microscope slides through a series of glass trays filled with solutions: 2 × 15 min Roti-clear.
Soak in 15 min 100% Ethanol.
Wash in 1 min 100% Ethanol.
Soak in 10 min 96% Ethanol.
Soak in 5 min 70% Ethanol.
Soak in 5 min 50% Ethanol.
Wash 3 × 5 min in PBS on the shaker at 100 r/min.
Place slides in thermostable chambers and add antigen retrieval solution (TRIS-EDTA pH 9.0 or Citrate pH 6.0).
Place chamber with slides in Steamer for 30 minutes at 100°C.
Allow slides to cool down to 20°C–25°C.
Permeabilize slides with 1% Triton X (in PBS) solution for 15 minutes.
Mark the area on the slides where organoids/tissue are located using a PAP pen liquid blocker.
Block slides with 100 μL of 10% donkey serum in dilution medium per slide.
Wash slides once with PBS.
Add primary antibodies in dilution medium, final volume 100 μL per slide.
Incubate slides for more than 16 hours at 4°C in a moist-filled incubation tray.
Add secondary antibodies in dilution medium, using 100 μL droplets per slide.
Incubate slides for 2 hours at 20°C–25°C.
Add DAPI diluted in dilution medium at 1:1000 and incubate for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Mount with Mowiol and place the coverslip.
Dry overnight to seal the slides with nail polish.
Image the prepared slides using a confocal microscope.
